the microstructure evolution of the Bi2CuO 4+20 wt% of Bi2O 3 samples quenched from 760–780 °C was studied and the conductivity of Bi2O4–Bi 2O 3 composites was measured in the temperature range of 660–790 ºC.

the microstructure evolution of the Bi2CuO3–Bi2O 3 composites was studied in detail by scanning electron microscopy and it was shown that the observed conductivity jump near 770 ºC can be explained in terms of grain boundary weting and formation of the grain boundary liquid channel structures.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the microstructural evolution and the effect of the Bi2O3 addition on the conductivity of Bi2O2CuO4 composites.
the study of microstructure evolution and electrical properties of Bi2Cu04–Bi2O 3 composites nearby their eutectic temperature.
the detailed investigation of grain boundary wet and dry states of Bi2Cu04–Bi2O 3 composites nearby 770 °C.
